title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 — hasso5703 SGLang lane with prefix caching
slug_note: The Flash-Next lane that actually makes prefix caching work on Spark: a 30K conversation re-served in 0.5 s warm versus 18.4 s cold.

variation.quant_detail: NVFP4 main weights, bf16 KV cache, 51B N-gram (PLE) table mmap-served from NVMe

engine.config: NEXTN/MTP speculative head, bf16 KV, PLE table mmap from NVMe, prefix caching on

requirements.notes: ~195 GB under $HOME (~136 GB checkpoint plus PLE table) plus Docker; host MemAvailable 16.6 GiB during a 120K prompt.

steps: Select the flash-next NVFP4 + MTP target
Keep the PLE table on NVMe; it is mmap-served, not loaded

measurements.method: two-call wall-clock decode, reasoning, single Spark
two-call wall-clock decode, free prose, single Spark
field report at ~100K context depth (user hashd1ve)
measurements.note: Stated as 'near 28-31' at depth; a depth point, not a fresh-context number.

measurements.method: 30K-token conversation re-served cold versus 0.5 s warm with prefix caching
measurements.note: The differentiator of this lane: prefix caching works here.

measurements.method: cold prefill with real QSA sparse kernels, stated ~1500-2000 tok/s
exact needle retrieval 9/9 at 120K prompt tokens; quality canaries 4/4
measurements.note: Retrieval canary at depth, not an intelligence index.

caveats: Overlaps the Mia, azampatti and blazux lanes on the same weights; the prefix-caching and 120K-retrieval numbers are what this lane adds.
Disk footprint is the real price: ~230 GB free, most of it the mmap-served PLE table.
